# OpenAPI documents generated by real frameworks

Each `*.json` here was generated by the framework itself from the small orders API under `apps/`, unedited. The apps
are the same API in every framework: a router or controller prefix, a path parameter, a POST, a route with an explicit
operationId (`orderHistory`) and a route hidden from the document. The tests read these documents to check that
flow-atlas understands what each framework actually emits.

| File | Framework (version used) | Document | How it was generated |
|---|---|---|---|
| `py-fastapi.json` | FastAPI 0.128.8 | OpenAPI 3.1.0 | `python apps/fastapi/main.py` (`app.openapi()`) |
| `py-smorest.json` | Flask 3.1.3, flask-smorest 0.46.2, apispec 6.8.4 | OpenAPI 3.0.3 | `python apps/flask-smorest/main.py` (`api.spec.to_dict()`) |
| `py-flasgger.json` | Flask 3.1.3, flasgger 0.9.7.1 | Swagger 2.0 | `python apps/flasgger/main.py` (test client, `/apispec_1.json`) |
| `py-drf.json` | Django 4.2.30, Django REST framework 3.16.1, drf-spectacular 0.30.0 | OpenAPI 3.0.3 | `python apps/django-drf/main.py` (`manage.py spectacular`) |
| `node-nest.json` | NestJS 11.1.24 (Fastify platform), @nestjs/swagger 11.4.7 | OpenAPI 3.0.0 | `apps/nestjs/main.ts` (`SwaggerModule.createDocument`) |
| `node-fastify-swagger.json` | Fastify 5.12.5, @fastify/swagger 9.8.1 | Swagger 2.0 | `node apps/fastify/main.cjs swagger` |
| `node-fastify-openapi.json` | Fastify 5.12.5, @fastify/swagger 9.8.1 | OpenAPI 3.0.3 | `node apps/fastify/main.cjs openapi` |
| `java-springdoc.json` | Spring Boot 3.5.6, springdoc-openapi 2.8.13 | OpenAPI 3.1.0 | `mvn test -Dout=…` in `apps/spring-springdoc` (MockMvc, `/v3/api-docs`) |

What they show:

- Every framework composes router, blueprint, controller and global prefixes itself; the document is the most
  complete list of routes a service serves.
- Default operationIds differ: FastAPI `read_order_api_v1_orders__order_id__get`, NestJS `OrdersController_read`,
  springdoc `read` (the method), drf-spectacular `api_v1_orders_retrieve`; flask-smorest, flasgger and Fastify give
  none unless the code states one.
- Some documents keep a trailing slash (`/api/v1/orders/` in DRF and in Fastify for a route registered as `/`).
- Documents leave routes out: hidden routes in every framework, and in flasgger every route without a YAML docstring.
- springdoc writes `servers` from the request it answered (`http://localhost`), so a server URL in a generated document
  belongs to the environment, not the code.
- No document says where a route is in the code, who calls it, or what its handler calls.
